Carmen (eng-platform): Heads-up: p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~2x over the last 45m. p50/p95 look fine. Heatmap shows spikes from a subset of pods. @Raj any recent routing rollouts?

Raj (eng-runtime): I rolled the route-tagging change in SmartRouter ~40m ago to add a route label (X-Route). Thought it only affected headers, not metrics. :eyes:

Carmen (eng-platform): That could explain it. Dashboards use an approx_quantile aggregation in the collector for endpoint-level percentiles. If the label was added mid-stream it might have changed series cardinality and skewed the p99.

Marta (observability): Quick note on queries — I noticed the dashboard panel uses an ad-hoc quantile_over_time on tDigest outputs. Example of what is running now: `quantile_over_time(0.99, collector_tdigest{endpoint="/v1/generate"}[1h])` — this is brittle when labels change. We should compute percentiles from merged histograms: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_latency_seconds_bucket{endpoint="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))`.

Raj (eng-runtime): Yikes. The header rewrite was meant to be low-risk. I can revert if needed.

Carmen (eng-platform): Before reverting, can we validate the hypothesis that tdigest merging + label churn produced the apparent tail drift? @metrics-bot can you pull raw histogram shards for the affected pods for the last 2 hours so we can compare exact vs approx?

metrics-bot: Pulled histograms for pods {pod-42,pod-45,pod-77}. Stored snapshots: /mnt/metrics/snapshots/176900_snapshots.tar.gz. Hash: abc123def. (I'll attach the diff in a follow-up message.)

Oliver (runtime): Checked SmartRouter logs — it set X-Route=variantA only for dedicated traffic. That creates a split: series that used to be one are now two. The collector was aggregating tDigests across series keys; changing keys mid-aggregation will distort the merged quantile. We should always merge histograms first, then extract quantiles.

Marta (observability): Action items I suggest: 1) update dashboard queries to use histogram_quantile with sum by (le, endpoint) so label churn doesn't change percentile math; 2) backfill endpoint-level aggregates from raw histograms for the last 12-24h to get a correct baseline; 3) update metrics-collector to prefer histogram merges over tDigest for endpoint-level SLO panels; 4) if customers are impacted, trigger a canary revert.

Raj (eng-runtime): I'll start a canary revert now and open a PR that scopes the new route label to internal traces only (not the metrics series keys).

Sam (product): Also for rollout UX: can we surface both "instance p99" and "endpoint p99" on the rollout page so PMs can quickly see whether tail regressions are per-instance or aggregated? That would reduce noisy alerts during label changes.

Carmen (eng-platform): Agree. For immediate fix, swap the dashboard panel query to this PromQL snippet:```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_latency_seconds_bucket{endpoint=\"/v1/generate\"}[5m])) by (le))
```This computes endpoint p99 from merged buckets.

Raj (eng-runtime): Running revert now. @deploy-bot start canary revert smart-router v2->v1 (3 pods).

deploy-bot: Canary revert triggered by Raj — rolling 3 pods now.

Marta (observability): I'll kick off a backfill job overnight and post a short report in this thread tomorrow morning with before/after graphs and a per-series count timeline to show cardinality change. For immediate visibility I added a temporary panel that shows the number of active series for /v1/generate over time.

Carmen (eng-platform): :thumbsup: Thanks everyone. Main takeaway: metric pipelines must compute percentiles from merged histograms at the logical endpoint level, not from merged sketches that are sensitive to label churn. I'll file a follow-up ticket to update dashboards and the collector with the plan Marta outlined.

Sam (product): Thanks — useful learnings for rollout docs too: note any metric/label consequences in the rollout checklist so we don't have surprise p99 spikes next time.

(End of thread)
